name: United Kingdom

legislature.name: House of Commons (650)
legislature.detail: Large majority from the July 2024 landslide; Reform UK leads many national polls.

legislature.name: House of Lords
legislature.detail: Appointed; hereditary peers being removed by 2025–26 legislation.

judiciary: Supreme Court of the United Kingdom; separate Scottish legal system.

elections.name: Scottish, Welsh & English local elections
elections.note: Heavy Labour losses triggered Starmer's exit.

synopsis: Keir Starmer resigned as Labour leader after disastrous May 2026 local elections; Andy Burnham, returning to Parliament via the Makerfield by-election, became Labour leader unopposed and Prime Minister in July 2026. He is trying to reset the government's direction against a strong challenge from Reform UK.
policies: Closer post-Brexit relations with the EU
Defence spending increase and support for Ukraine
challenges: Weak polling and rise of Reform UK
Union tensions after the 2026 Scottish and Welsh elections
reviewNote: Confirm Burnham's appointment date and cabinet.

name: Ireland

legislature.name: Dáil Éireann (174)
legislature.detail: Sinn Féin is the main opposition.

judiciary: Supreme Court of Ireland.

elections.name: General election (latest)
elections.note: Simon Harris (FG) due to rotate in as Taoiseach in Nov 2027.

synopsis: A centre-right Fianna Fáil–Fine Gael coalition governs with independent support, with a planned rotation of Taoiseach to Simon Harris in late 2027.
challenges: Exposure to US tariffs and pharma/tech firms

name: France

legislature.name: National Assembly (577)
legislature.detail: Left alliance, Macron's centrists and the RN–allies bloc each lack a majority; governments survive via abstentions.

judiciary: Constitutional Council, Court of Cassation and Council of State.

elections.name: Presidential election (1st round)
elections.note: Macron is term-limited; Marine Le Pen barred pending appeal, Jordan Bardella RN's likely candidate.

synopsis: France has cycled through prime ministers since the 2024 snap election produced a hung parliament. Budget consolidation and the 2027 presidential succession dominate.
policies: Pension reform (partially suspended as a concession)
European defence and support for Ukraine
challenges: High deficit and debt; rating downgrades
reviewNote: Prime minister status not verified for 2026 — confirm.

name: Germany

legislature.name: Bundestag (630)
legislature.detail: AfD is the largest opposition party.

legislature.name: Bundesrat (69)
legislature.control: Represents state governments; no fixed majority

judiciary: Federal Constitutional Court (Karlsruhe) with strong judicial review.

elections.name: State elections (BW, RP, ST, MV, Berlin)

synopsis: Merz leads a grand coalition with the SPD after loosening the debt brake for defence and infrastructure. The government is trying to revive a stagnant economy while the AfD polls strongly.
policies: €500bn infrastructure fund and exemption of defence from the debt brake
Military expansion and new military service model
challenges: AfD strength, especially in the east
Coalition friction on welfare and pensions

name: Netherlands

legislature.name: House of Representatives (150)
legislature.detail: Needs opposition support bill by bill; PVV and GL–PvdA lead the opposition.

judiciary: Supreme Court; Dutch courts cannot review laws for constitutionality.

elections.name: General election
elections.note: D66 narrowly edged out the PVV.

synopsis: Rob Jetten, the youngest PM in Dutch history, leads a centrist minority cabinet that must negotiate every bill. Planned health and welfare savings face strong opposition.

name: Belgium
judiciary: Constitutional Court, Court of Cassation, Council of State.
synopsis: Flemish nationalist De Wever leads a five-party centre-right coalition focused on budget repair and labour-market reform.

name: Luxembourg
judiciary: Constitutional Court and Superior Court of Justice.
synopsis: A centre-right CSV–DP government governs a wealthy financial centre; Grand Duke Guillaume succeeded his father Henri in October 2025.

name: Austria

legislature.name: National Council (183)
legislature.detail: FPÖ is the largest party but in opposition.

judiciary: Constitutional Court, Supreme Court, Administrative Court.
synopsis: Austria's first three-party coalition formed after talks between the FPÖ and ÖVP collapsed. It is focused on budget consolidation and migration control, while the FPÖ leads polls.
policies: Budget consolidation to exit EU excessive-deficit procedure
Pause on family reunification for refugees

name: Switzerland
system: Federal directorial republic with direct democracy
judiciary: Federal Supreme Court (no review of federal laws' constitutionality).
synopsis: Switzerland's consensus 'magic formula' government shares power among the four largest parties. Debate centres on the new EU bilateral package and US tariffs.
policies: New bilateral treaty package with the EU
challenges: Referendums on EU deal and population cap ('10 million' initiative)
Export pressure from strong franc and tariffs

name: Liechtenstein
system: Constitutional monarchy with strong princely powers and direct democracy

headOfState.name: Hans-Adam II (Hereditary Prince Alois as regent)
headOfState.title: Prince

judiciary: State Court (constitutional) and Supreme Court.
synopsis: Liechtenstein's first female prime minister leads the traditional two-party coalition.

name: Monaco

legislature.name: National Council (24)
legislature.control: Monaco Nationale / Primo! Priorité Monaco (all seats in 2023)

judiciary: Supreme Court.
synopsis: Executive power rests with the Prince and his appointed Minister of State; the elected National Council approves budgets and laws.

name: Andorra

headOfState.name: Emmanuel Macron and Bishop Josep-Lluís Serrano Pentinat
headOfState.title: Co-Princes

judiciary: Constitutional Tribunal and Superior Court of Justice.
synopsis: Espot's centre-right government is finalising an association agreement with the EU and tackling housing pressures.

name: Italy

headOfGovernment.name: Giorgia Meloni
headOfGovernment.title: President of the Council of Ministers

judiciary: Constitutional Court; a constitutional reform separating judges' and prosecutors' careers has been central to government–judiciary tension.
synopsis: Meloni leads one of Italy's most stable post-war governments, combining fiscal prudence with conservative social and migration policy and an Atlanticist foreign policy.
policies: Fiscal discipline to exit EU deficit procedure
Support for Ukraine and close ties with the US
challenges: Low growth and high public debt

name: San Marino

headOfState.name: Two Captains Regent (rotate every 6 months, 1 Apr / 1 Oct)
headOfState.title: Captains Regent

headOfGovernment.name: Congress of State (Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs: Luca Beccari)
headOfGovernment.title: Collective government

judiciary: Guarantors' College (constitutional) and courts.
synopsis: San Marino is governed by a PDCS-led coalition and finalising an association agreement with the EU.
reviewNote: Update names of current Captains Regent each April and October.

name: Vatican City

headOfGovernment.name: Sr. Raffaella Petrini (Governorate); Cardinal Pietro Parolin (Secretary of State)
headOfGovernment.title: President of the Governorate / Secretary of State

legislature.name: Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State

judiciary: Vatican tribunals; the Pope holds supreme judicial power.
synopsis: Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope, has emphasised continuity with Francis on social issues while seeking unity within the Church.
policies: Financial reform of the Holy See

name: Spain

legislature.name: Congress of Deputies (350)
legislature.detail: Minority government lost key housing votes after Junts withdrew support.

judiciary: Constitutional Court and Supreme Court; corruption probes touch PSOE figures.

elections.name: Snap general election
elections.note: Called on 5 Oct 2026; polls favour PP, possibly with Vox.

synopsis: Sánchez called a snap election for 29 November 2026 after parliament rejected his housing decrees. The Socialists trail the People's Party in polls.
reviewNote: Snap election on 29 Nov 2026 — update result.

name: Portugal

legislature.name: Assembly of the Republic (230)
legislature.detail: Chega became the second-largest party in May 2025.

judiciary: Constitutional Court and Supreme Court of Justice.
synopsis: Montenegro's centre-right minority government faces a fragmented parliament with a strong far-right Chega, while a Socialist president was elected in 2026.
policies: Tax cuts and housing supply measures

name: Malta

legislature.name: House of Representatives
legislature.detail: Nationalist Party (led by Alex Borg) in opposition.

judiciary: Constitutional Court and Court of Appeal.

elections.name: General election
elections.note: Labour's record fourth straight win (~52%), with a narrower margin.

synopsis: Abela secured a third term as PM in May 2026, with Labour winning a record fourth consecutive election.

name: Greece
judiciary: Supreme Civil and Criminal Court, Council of State.
synopsis: Mitsotakis's single-party government has overseen economic recovery and rating upgrades but is weakened by the Tempi rail-disaster fallout and a subsidy scandal.

name: Cyprus

governingParties: Independent president backed by DIKO and others

legislature.name: House of Representatives (56)
legislature.detail: May 2026: DISY 17, AKEL 15, ELAM 8, DIKO 8, ALMA 4, Direct Democracy 4.

judiciary: Supreme Constitutional Court and Supreme Court.

elections.name: Parliamentary election
elections.note: Far-right ELAM became joint third; new outsider parties entered.

synopsis: Christodoulides holds Cyprus's EU Council presidency in the first half of 2026 and faces a fragmented House after ELAM's surge.
challenges: Cyprus problem / division of the island
